A.text: Management of a natal or neonatal tooth should take into account any medical or contributing factors.

cites.section: Perinatal and Infant Oral Health Care › Anticipatory guidance

B.text: Medical factors are to be considered in management, so saying they have no bearing is wrong.

cites.section: Perinatal and Infant Oral Health Care › Anticipatory guidance

C.text: Routine removal in every case ignores the instruction to weigh the infant's medical and contributing factors.

cites.section: Perinatal and Infant Oral Health Care › Anticipatory guidance

D.text: Contributing factors must be considered, so relying on mobility alone is incorrect.

cites.section: Perinatal and Infant Oral Health Care › Anticipatory guidance

explanation.text: Clinicians managing a natal or neonatal tooth should consider medical or contributing factors, which makes the medical evaluation part of the decision.
